method: least squares of green pit time on the following green stint length and a tyre-change indicator, per class, trimmed at 3x the class median

GTD.why_not: 62% of stops are followed by a near-full tank (90% or more of 30 laps), so this race is run on full fills and the fill size barely varies. The split between what a stop costs to enter and what it costs to fill is not identifiable from a sample where almost nothing but a full fill was ever taken - not by this fit, and not by a quantile either. **This supersedes any bound below.**

GTDPRO.why_not: the fill proxy explains nothing: the slope is -0.17 s a lap with t = -0.8 and R2 = 0.004, so it cannot be told from zero. The intercept then absorbs the whole cost of an average stop, which is why it comes out at 1.04 of one - that number is the mean, not the lane
GTDPRO.tyre_note: tyres changed at effectively every stop or none, so the tyre term is not identified and is left out of the fit - the same condition `deg_identified` reports for degradation
